text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Greek side announces unilateral suspension of Greek military flights over Cyprus.
- United Nations proximity talks between the two sides are put on hold for two weeks while chief of mission Gustave Feissel has consultations in New York.
- Greek and Turkish Cypriot women who met in Brussels last week decide to set up a "Cyprus Link" to promote contacts between the two sides.
- Two people die in car crash.
- The government is reconsidering the levels of excise duties on imported cars.
- Two football clubs are heading towards privatisation to solve their cash problems.
- The Cyprus Trading Company proposes a seven percent dividend in its 1996 results.
- Communist Akel party leader Demetris Christofias calls on President Glafcos Clerides to clarify his position regarding the Cyprus issue.

- The National Council (advisory body on the Cyprus issue comprised of party leaders) meets today amid tension and complaints from party leaders that Clerides kept them in the dark concerning developments on the Cyprus problem.
- President Clerides appears determined to clarify his position concerning the current phase of the Cyprus issue at the National Council meeting today.
- The government officially admitted yesterday it had shelved the (common defence) doctrine with Greece and accepted a ban on military overflights.
